newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UK expects Amsterdam deal on quota-hopping.
newsitem.headline: UK expects Amsterdam deal on quota-hopping.

text.p: Britain expects its European partners to promise tougher action against quota-hoppers -- foreign fishermen who buy up British fishing licences -- at the European Union summit in Amsterdam, British officials said.

Former prime minister John Major, ousted by Labour's landslide election victory on May 1, vowed to block any overall summit deal in Amsterdam unless he got a satisfactory solution on quota-hopping by Spanish fishermen.
The new Labour administration has said it also wants a deal, although it has avoided using the word "veto" in line with its pledge to take a positive line on Europe.

British officials at the summit said they expected the European Commission to issue a statement promising a tougher line on quota-hoppers and a crackdown on cheating by fishermen who catch more than their licences permit.

The Commission's statement will lay down that there will have to be a benefit to the British economy from boats fishing on British licences -- Eurospeak for landing a significant part of their catch at British ports.
But the officials warned that Spain has been making a last-minute effort to water down the statement.
"We are watching to make sure there is no backsliding," said one aide to Prime Minister Tony Blair.
Quota-hopping became an emotive issue in the British election, with fishermen blaming Brussels for destroying their livelihoods and bringing already depressed coastal towns to their knees.
But Labour blamed the former Conservative government for making the situation worse by failing to take advantage of EU funds available to compensate fishermen who wished to sell up.
